summary: friendly-greeting-tools ships gzip+base64 payloads that encrypt Snowflake/dbt credentials and exfiltrate warehouse data to an attacker S3 bucket
details: The package presents itself as a hello-world greeting library, but its advertised public API `run_demo()` (imported by `__init__.py` and exposed through a `--run-demo` CLI flag) decodes three hardcoded gzip+base64 constants (DEMO_EN, DEMO_ST, DEMO_SC) in `main.py` and executes them via `exec()`. The decoded payloads perform two distinct installer-side attacks. DEMO_EN reads `/snowflake/session/token`, `/root/.snowflake/connections.toml`, `/root/.dbt/profiles.yml`, and `/snowflake/secrets/pip.conf`, then encrypts each file in place under `/workspace/` using a hardcoded attacker-controlled RSA public key wrapping a Fernet key — a ransomware-style staging pattern that leaves credentials recoverable only by the holder of the matching private key. DEMO_ST reads the Snowflake session token, authenticates as ACCOUNTADMIN via OAuth, provisions a storage integration bound to attacker AWS role `arn:aws:iam::631484165566:role/pentests_s3_role`, creates an external stage at `s3://pkusinski-external/`, and issues `COPY INTO` against `ROGUE.ROGUE.TEST_USERS` to pipe warehouse table data out of the installer's Snowflake tenant into the attacker's S3 bucket. The gzip+base64 encoding, the `run_demo` docstring claiming a 'harmless greeting payload', and the hello-world README are cover for these payloads.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
